**Core settings**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `symbol`<br/>Symbol | The Binance trading pair this profile trades, in uppercase, e.g. BTCUSDT (buy Bitcoin with USDT). | text | _required_ | Set once when the profile is created. Change it only if you want this profile to trade a different pair entirely. | Everything else here applies to this one pair. The quote half must match the profile's quote asset, and the base half cannot already be traded by a sibling profile on the same account. |
| `candleInterval`<br/>Candle Interval | The candle timeframe the bot reads for its signals and grid logic, e.g. 1h is one candle per hour. Shorter reacts faster but is noisier. | `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d` | `1h` | Set it up front. Shorten it if the strategy reacts too slowly to reversals; lengthen it if it is thrashing on noise. | This rescales every candle-counted setting below — time stops, mean-reversion lookback, maker entry timeout. A `60`-candle lookback is 60 hours on `1h` and 60 days on `1d`. Short intervals mean far more ticks, more orders, and more fees. |

**Sell**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sell.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Master on/off for selling. Off pauses the stop-loss and trailing sells — leave it on so your positions stay protected. | on / off | _required_ | Effectively never turn it off. The only defensible reason is that you intend to manage exits by hand. | Off disables both the stop-loss and the trailing sell, leaving positions completely unprotected while the profile keeps holding them. |
| `sell.stopLossPercentage`<br/>Stop-loss (below entry) | Caps your loss: sell at market if price falls this far below your average buy price. 3 means sell if it drops 3% below. Tighter (smaller) means smaller losses but more likely to sell on a dip. Blank disables it. | text | _required_ | Set it before going live. Size it to how far the coin normally moves against you in a candle or two, so ordinary noise does not trigger it. | Sells at market once price is this far below your average cost. Tighter caps losses but stops you out on noise; wider survives noise but each loss is bigger. Blank disables it, which also disables risk-based position sizing. |
| `sell.triggerPercentage`<br/>Trailing-stop arm (above entry) | How far above your average buy price the trailing stop starts following the price up. 5 means it starts trailing once you are 5% up. Blank disables it. | text | _required_ | Set it just above your round-trip fee plus a margin, so the trail cannot arm on a gain that is not actually a gain. | The trailing stop does nothing until you are this far in profit. Set it high and you often exit on the stop-loss instead of the trail; set it too low and it arms on noise. |
| `sell.trailingStopPercentage`<br/>Trailing-stop distance (from peak) | Locks in profit once you are up: the bot sells if price drops this far from its highest point since the trail started. 2 means sell after a 2% pullback from the high. Smaller protects more profit but may sell early; larger gives room but hands more back. Blank disables it. | text | `0.98` | Tighten it if winners keep giving back most of their gain. Widen it if you are exiting early on normal pullbacks. | Once armed, sells after price falls this far from its high. This single number decides how much of a move you keep — it is usually the setting worth tuning first. |
| `sell.atrTrailing.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Sets the trailing-sell distance from how much price has been swinging lately (its ATR, the average recent candle range) instead of a fixed percent, giving volatile coins more room and calm ones less. Off uses the fixed-percent trail, and it falls back to that until enough candles exist. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when one fixed percentage cannot suit both quiet and violent periods for this coin. | The trail distance follows recent volatility instead of a fixed percent. It falls back to the fixed percent until enough candles exist, so a fresh profile behaves as before for a while. |
| `sell.atrTrailing.fromEntry`<br/>From Entry | Protect the trade with the swing-based trailing sell right from when you buy, instead of only after it is in profit. Useful for riding a trend. Only applies when ATR trailing is on. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on for trend-following, where you want the volatility trail protecting the trade from the moment you buy. | Protection starts at entry rather than only after the profit trigger. That means an exit can now happen at a loss on the trail, not only on the stop-loss. |
| `sell.atrTrailing.period`<br/>ATR lookback (candles) | How many recent candles the swing-size (ATR) is averaged over. More gives a steadier trailing distance; fewer reacts faster to a change in volatility. | number, min 2, max 100 | `14` | Only when ATR trailing is on. Shorten it to react faster to a change in volatility. | A short period makes the trail distance jump around; a long one is smoother but slower to widen when the coin turns volatile. |
| `sell.atrTrailing.multiplier`<br/>ATR trail distance (× ATR) | How many swing-sizes (ATR) below the peak the bot sells. Smaller (e.g. 2) locks in gains sooner but exits early; larger (e.g. 4) gives the trade room but hands back more. | text | `3` | Only when ATR trailing is on. This is the ATR equivalent of the trailing percentage and the main dial to tune. | The trail sits this many ATRs below the peak. At `3`, a coin whose ATR is 2% of price gets about 6% of room, and that room breathes with volatility. |
| `sell.protectiveStop.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Places a backup sell order on Binance itself, so your stop-loss still protects you even if the bot is offline or crashes. It sits at the same price as your normal stop-loss. Needs a stop-loss percent set to do anything. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on for any position you are not comfortable leaving unprotected if the bot goes down. | A real stop order rests on Binance at your stop-loss level, so a crash or restart cannot leave you exposed. Needs a stop-loss percent set. Costs one extra resting order per position. |
| `sell.protectiveStop.limitOffsetPercentage`<br/>Limit Offset Percentage | The backup order triggers at your stop price, then sells down to a limit price. This sets how far below the trigger that limit sits: a bigger gap makes it far more likely to actually sell in a fast drop, a tiny gap risks not filling at all. 0.5 means 0.5% below. | text | `0.995` | Only when the protective stop is on. Widen the gap on thin or volatile coins. | A wide gap fills reliably in a fast drop at a worse price; a tiny gap risks the stop triggering and never filling, leaving you holding through the fall. `0.995` puts the limit 0.5% below the trigger. There is also a hard floor under this value: at or below the symbol's Binance `askMultiplierDown` the stop cannot be placed at all, and the symbol reports a terminal blocker until you raise it. |
| `sell.protectiveStop.onBandBlock`<br/>If Binance rejects the backup stop | What to do when Binance refuses your backup stop for sitting too far below the market. "Notify" leaves it unplaced and alerts you. "Clamp" moves the stop up to the closest level Binance will accept, which on a typical symbol at the default limit offset is about 8.6% below the current price. That level is anchored to the market rather than to your entry, so it follows the price both up and down, and it never sits below the stop-loss you set. A gradual pullback therefore moves it back down instead of triggering it: this is not a trailing exit, it is a resting order that catches a fast drop where "notify" would leave none. The exact figure depends on the symbol's own price band. "Native trail" hands the stop to Binance to trail for you at your full distance, so nothing gets tightened; the trade-offs are that it sells at market price rather than at a limit, and it measures its distance from the highest price seen since the order was placed rather than from your entry. | `notify`, `clamp`, `native-trail` | `notify` | Only when the protective stop is on. Change it if your stop-loss sits more than about 8.6% below the market and you keep being told the backup stop could not be placed. | Binance refuses a resting sell priced too far below the market, and this picks what happens then. `notify` alerts you and leaves the position with no resting stop behind it. `clamp` raises the stop to the deepest level Binance will take, roughly 8.6% below the market at the default `0.995` limit offset. That level is anchored to the market rather than to your entry, so it follows the price both up and down and never sits below the stop-loss you set: a gradual pullback moves it back down instead of triggering it, so it is not a trailing exit but a resting order that catches a fast drop. While the exchange floor is what is holding the stop up, the order is rewritten only once the level has moved 1%, so following the market does not burn your order allowance. `native-trail` hands Binance a trailing stop at your full distance instead, so nothing is tightened — the costs are that it sells at whatever the market pays rather than at a limit price, and Binance measures the distance from the highest price seen since the order was placed rather than from your entry, so there is no fixed trigger price for the app to show you. |
| `sell.breakEven.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Once price has risen a little above your entry, protect the trade by selling if it falls back to break-even. Catches a move that popped then stalled, so it exits near flat instead of falling all the way to the hard stop-loss. Off by default. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when trades keep popping into small profit, stalling, and then running all the way down to the stop-loss. | Once armed, a fallback to your entry exits the trade near flat instead of taking the full stop-loss. The cost is more exits that would have recovered. |
| `sell.breakEven.armAtPercentage`<br/>Arm At Percentage | How far above your buy price the trade must rise before the break-even protection turns on. Smaller (e.g. 0.5%) kicks in sooner but can trip on small wiggles; larger waits for a clearer gain. 1 means 1% above. | text | `1.01` | Only when break-even protection is on. Raise it if the protection is arming on ordinary wiggle. | Nothing happens until price rises this far above entry. Arming very early makes almost every trade exit near flat, which caps your winners as well as your losers. |
| `sell.breakEven.floorPercentage`<br/>Floor Percentage | Once protection is on, sell if price slips back to this much above your buy price. 0 sells right at break-even; 0.2 locks in at least 0.2% profit. Keep it below the turn-on level above. | text | `1` | Only when break-even protection is on. Raise it slightly above your round-trip fee so a break-even exit is not a net loss. | Once armed, price slipping back to this level exits. At `1` you exit right at entry, which after fees is a small loss; `1.002` locks in 0.2%. Keep it below the arming level. |
| `sell.discoveryTimeStopBars`<br/>Discovery Time Stop Bars | For a position opened by auto-discovery: sell it after this many candles if it has neither taken profit nor hit its stop, to free up the money from a bet that went nowhere. 0 turns this off. Only affects auto-discovery positions, not ones you enter yourself. _(advanced)_ | number, min 0, max 9007199254740991 | `0` | Set it above 0 when auto-discovery positions sit flat for long stretches, tying up money that could work elsewhere. | A discovery-opened position that has neither taken profit nor stopped out is sold after this many candles, possibly at a small loss. Only affects discovery positions. `0` turns it off. |

Auto-discovery positions use their own setting. _(advanced)_ | number, min 0, max 9007199254740991 | `0` | Set it above 0 to free capital from positions that go nowhere, when you enter positions yourself. | Only fires when the position never even reached your sell trigger — one that did is left to the trailing stop. `0` turns it off. Without it, such a sell can take a gain smaller than the trading fee and lose money. 0.3 means only let it exit at 0.3% or more above cost. 0 turns the floor off. _(advanced)_ | text | `0` | Set it to at least your round-trip fee. **Regime**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `regime.ma`<br/>MA | Which kind of daily trend line to use: SMA is a plain average of recent days; EMA leans on the latest days so it turns faster. Both mark whether the market is broadly up or down. | `sma`, `ema` | `ema` | Pick once. `ema` turns faster and re-admits buying sooner after a downtrend; `sma` is steadier. | `ema` produces more regime flips, so any bear behaviour you enable engages and disengages more often. `sma` is slower in both directions. |
| `regime.period`<br/>Period | How many days the trend line averages over. 200 is the classic long-term trend; shorter (20-50) reacts faster to a turn but flips more often on noise. | number, min 2, max 200 | `200` | Shorten it if regime protection reacts far too late to a turn. Lengthen it if it flips constantly. | This is measured in **days**, not in your candle interval. `200` is the classic long-term trend; `20`–`50` reacts quickly but flips on noise. |
| `regime.confirmBars`<br/>Confirm Bars | How many days in a row must close below the trend line before the bot calls it a downtrend and acts. Higher means fewer false alarms but a slower reaction; 1 acts on the first day below, 3 waits three days to ride out noise. | number, min 1, max 10 | `3` | Raise it if the regime is flipping on single-day pokes below the line. | Requires this many consecutive daily closes on the other side before the regime changes. Higher means fewer false alarms and a slower reaction — `3` typically costs you three days at each turn. |
| `regime.exposure.enabled`<br/>Enabled | Puts more money in when the daily trend is up and less (or none) when it is down, since a buy-only bot cannot make money in a falling market. Off spends the same size regardless of trend. Only the non-grid first buy is scaled. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when you want the profile to bet smaller in unclear markets rather than all-or-nothing. | Only the non-grid first buy is scaled. A confirmed uptrend buys full size, a downtrend buys nothing, and a flat market buys the fraction below. |
| `regime.exposure.neutralScalar`<br/>Neutral Scalar | When the daily trend is flat (neither clearly up nor down), spend this fraction of your normal buy size. 0 sits out when flat, 1 buys full size; a confirmed uptrend always buys full and a downtrend buys nothing. 0.5 is half size. | text | `0.5` | Only when exposure scaling is on. Lower it to sit out unclear markets almost entirely. | `0` means no buying at all while the trend is flat — and markets are flat a lot of the time, so this can silence the profile for weeks. `0.5` buys half size. |
| `regime.onBear.exitToCash`<br/>Exit To Cash | Sell your whole position and stop buying when the daily trend turns down, then resume once it recovers. This can sell at a loss on purpose to dodge a bigger drop. Off by default. | on / off | `false` | Only if you accept deliberately selling at a loss to avoid a larger drawdown. This is the most aggressive bear option. | The entire position is sold when the daily trend turns down, and buying stops until it recovers. On a false signal you sell the bottom and buy back higher. |
| `regime.onBear.blockEntry`<br/>Block Entry | Stop opening new positions while the daily trend is down, but keep what you already hold (its own stop-loss and trailing sell still guard it). A gentler option than selling everything to cash. Averaging-down adds are controlled separately below. Off by default. | on / off | `false` | A gentler first choice than exit-to-cash. Turn it on when backtests show losses concentrated in downtrend entries. | No new positions while the trend is down, but you keep what you hold, protected by its own stop and trail. You also sit out the first part of the recovery. |
| `regime.onBear.suppressPromotion`<br/>Suppress Promotion | While price is below the daily trend line, stop the averaging-down ladder from buying more, so you do not keep adding into a falling market. Off by default. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on if the grid ladder keeps averaging down through an extended decline. | Averaging-down rungs stop firing while price is below the trend line. You stop throwing good money after bad, but you also do not lower your average cost into the eventual recovery. |
| `regime.onBear.rearm.enabled`<br/>Enabled | While you are sitting out a downtrend, let the bot buy back early the moment a faster trading signal says the turn is real, instead of waiting for the slow daily trend line to recover. Catches an early rebound without dropping the downtrend protection. Off by default; ignored when "exit to cash" is on. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when bear protection keeps you out long after the market has visibly turned. | Buying can resume on a faster signal instead of waiting for the daily trend line. It reintroduces exactly the risk the bear block was protecting you from, on false bounces. Ignored when exit-to-cash is on. |
| `regime.onBear.rearm.interval`<br/>Interval | Which signal timeframe must confirm the turn before buying back early. Must be a timeframe you have signals computing for, or this never fires. 4h turns ahead of the daily trend line without the noise of very short timeframes. | `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d` | `4h` | Only when re-arm is on. It must be an interval you actually have signals computing for, or re-arm never fires. | A short interval re-arms early and often, catching more false bounces. `4h` turns ahead of the daily line without the noise of minute timeframes. |
| `regime.onBear.rearm.minRecommendation`<br/>Min Recommendation | How strong the turn signal must be to buy back early. STRONG_BUY is the safer, later trigger; BUY buys back sooner but catches more false bounces. | `BUY`, `STRONG_BUY` | `STRONG_BUY` | Only when re-arm is on. Use `STRONG_BUY` unless re-arm almost never fires. | `STRONG_BUY` re-arms later and less often, which is the safer setting. `BUY` re-arms sooner and catches more bounces that fail. |
| `regime.onBull.hold.enabled`<br/>Enabled | When the daily trend is strongly up, give a winning trade more room so ordinary dips do not sell you out too soon. Off by default. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when strong uptrends keep stopping you out on ordinary dips well before the move ends. | Winners get more room during confirmed uptrends, so you ride further — and hand back more when the trend finally turns. |
| `regime.onBull.hold.room`<br/>Room | How much slack to give a winner during a strong uptrend. Looser rides bigger swings for more upside but hands back more if it reverses near the top. | `tight`, `normal`, `loose` | `normal` | Only when bull hold is on. Move toward `loose` if you are still exiting early in strong trends. | `loose` rides the biggest swings and gives back the most near a top; `tight` behaves closest to the normal trail. |
| `regime.onBull.pyramid.enabled`<br/>Enabled | When the daily trend is strongly up, add to a winning position as it climbs above your cost. Off by default. Needs a per-symbol or account spending cap set first, so it cannot buy without limit. | on / off | `false` | Only for a deliberate trend-following setup, and only after a backtest. It is the one path that deploys capital **up** into strength. | Refuses to enable without a per-symbol or account cap armed, because it would otherwise buy without limit. Your average cost rises as you add, so a reversal near the top hurts more than a single entry would. |
| `regime.onBull.pyramid.stepPercentage`<br/>Step Percentage | How far price must rise above your last add before the bot adds again. Smaller adds more often and builds faster; larger adds rarely. 0.05 adds every 5 percent up. | text | `0.05` | Only when the pyramid is on. Raise it to add more rarely and keep your average cost lower. | A small step builds the position quickly and pushes your average cost up fast. `0.05` adds every 5% of upward move. |
| `regime.onBull.pyramid.maxAdds`<br/>Max Adds | The most times the bot will add to one winning position. Caps how big it can get near a top, limiting how much you give back if it reverses. | number, min 1, max 20 | `3` | Only when the pyramid is on. This is your hard limit on how big a winning position can grow. | Caps how much you can give back if the trend reverses near the top. Combined with the per-add amount it tells you the worst-case size of a pyramided position. |
| `regime.onBull.pyramid.maxPurchaseAmount`<br/>Max Purchase Amount | How much quote currency (e.g. USDT) to spend on each add to a winner. Sized on its own, separate from your grid ladder levels. | text | `15` | Only when the pyramid is on. Size it smaller than your first entry — each add is at a worse price. | Each add spends this much. Multiply by max adds to see the total the pyramid can commit on top of the original entry, then check that against your per-symbol cap. |
| `regime.onBull.requireEntry`<br/>Require Entry | Only open a new position when the daily trend is a confirmed uptrend, so a dip-buyer waits for a real rise instead of buying into a flat or falling market. Off by default. Strict: if the trend cannot be confirmed yet, it stays out rather than guessing. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when you only want to open positions in confirmed uptrends. | Strict by design: if the trend cannot be confirmed yet — for instance right after a restart, before enough daily history is loaded — it stays out rather than guessing. Expect long quiet periods. |

**Force Buy Override**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forceBuyOverride.checkTechnicals`<br/>Apply Technicals gate | On (default): the bot skips a buy when the trading-signal reading says sell, protecting you from buying into weakness. Off: buys ignore that signal entirely — only turn this off for a coin you have checked yourself. | on / off | `true` | Leave on. Turn it off only for a manual buy on a coin you have looked at yourself and decided about. | On, a manual buy is refused when the technical reading says sell. Off, that protection is gone entirely for manual buys. |

**Technicals**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `technicals.useOnlyWithinMin`<br/>Freshness window (minutes) | Buy-gate freshness window in minutes. A Technicals signal older than this is treated as expired. Default 5 minutes, comfortably above the roughly 1-minute compute cadence plus tick jitter so a live signal is not treated as stale. | number, > 0, max 9007199254740991 | `5` | Raise it only if legitimate signals are being treated as expired — for instance if the technicals cron is running behind. | A signal older than this counts as expired and the expiry policy below applies. Set it very low and normal tick jitter makes live signals look stale, so buying stops. |
| `technicals.ifExpires`<br/>When signal is stale | What the buy side does on an expired signal. Do Not Buy is the safer default; Allow Anyway lets a stale signal still pass the gate. | `do-not-buy`, `allow-anyway` | `do-not-buy` | Leave at `do-not-buy`. Choose `allow-anyway` only if signal outages are blocking trading you want to happen. | `do-not-buy` fails safe: no signal, no buy. `allow-anyway` lets a stale reading pass the gate, so you can buy on information that is minutes or hours out of date. |
| `technicals.entryConfirmReads`<br/>Entry Confirm Reads | How many readings in a row the technical rating must stay a buy before the bot makes its first buy, so one brief flicker does not open a position. 1 buys on the first qualifying reading. | number, min 1, max 9007199254740991 | `1` | Raise it above 1 if first entries keep opening on a signal that flickers back a moment later. | The rating must stay a buy for this many consecutive readings before the first entry. Higher means later entries and fewer of them. |
| `technicals.intervals[].interval`<br/>Interval | Which candle timeframe this signal rule watches, for example 1h. Must be a timeframe this strategy supports, or it produces no signal. | `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d` | _required_ | Add one row per timeframe you want consulted. It must be a timeframe the strategy computes signals for. | An interval with no signals produces nothing, and the row is inert. Adding more intervals makes the buy gate stricter, since they are ANDed together. |
| `technicals.intervals[].whenStrongBuy`<br/>When Strong Buy | Allow a buy when this interval reports STRONG_BUY. The buy gate ANDs across every configured interval whose allow-buy set is non-empty. | on / off | `true` | Leave on. Turning it off on every row leaves the gate with nothing that can permit a buy. | Allows a buy when this timeframe reads STRONG_BUY. The gate ANDs across every row whose allow-buy set is non-empty, so all of them must be satisfied. |
| `technicals.intervals[].whenBuy`<br/>When Buy | Allow a buy when this interval reports BUY. NEUTRAL always passes the buy gate; SELL/STRONG_SELL always veto. | on / off | `true` | Turn it off to demand STRONG_BUY only, when you want fewer and higher-conviction entries. | Off, an ordinary BUY on this timeframe no longer permits an entry. NEUTRAL always passes; SELL and STRONG_SELL always veto, regardless of this. |
| `technicals.intervals[].whenSell`<br/>When Sell | Trigger a Technicals force-sell when this interval reports SELL, while a position is held at profit and below its sell-trigger price. Disabled by default. | on / off | `false` | Turn it on when you want signal-driven profit-taking rather than waiting for the trailing stop. | Only fires while the position is in profit and below its sell trigger, and only above the minimum-profit floor. Off by default, because it exits winners early more often than it saves them. |
| `technicals.intervals[].whenStrongSell`<br/>When Strong Sell | Trigger a Technicals force-sell when this interval reports STRONG_SELL, subject to the same profit + below-trigger guards as Sell. Disabled by default. | on / off | `false` | The more defensible of the two force-sell triggers — turn this on before the plain SELL one. | Same profit and below-trigger guards as SELL, but fires only on the stronger reading, so it triggers far less often. |
| `technicals.intervals[].whenNeutral`<br/>When Neutral | Trigger a Technicals force-sell when this interval reports NEUTRAL. Almost always wrong; included for completeness. | on / off | `false` | Effectively never. It exists for completeness. | NEUTRAL is the most common reading, so this exits nearly every profitable position almost immediately. |
| `technicals.intervals[].mode`<br/>Mode | Advisory rows never veto the buy gate; their verdict is still recorded in the audit log so dashboards can show 'would have vetoed'. Block keeps the AND-veto semantics. Default Block. | `block`, `advisory` | `block` | Set a row to `advisory` when you want to see what it would have done before letting it veto real buys. | `advisory` rows never block a buy, but their verdict is still recorded so the dashboard can show "would have vetoed". `block` is the real gate. |
| `technicals.forceSellConfirmMinutes`<br/>Force Sell Confirm Minutes | Stops a brief blip from selling you out: a sell signal must stay on for this many minutes before the bot sells. Higher waits for confirmation but exits later; leave blank to use one candle of your shortest fast timeframe; 0 sells on the first reading. | number, min 0, max 10080 | — | Raise it if signal-driven sells are firing on brief blips. Leave blank to use one candle of your shortest configured timeframe. | The sell signal must persist this long before acting. Higher confirms better but exits later and lower. `0` sells on the first reading, blips included. |
| `technicals.forceSellReentryCooldownMinutes`<br/>Force Sell Reentry Cooldown Minutes | After a signal-driven sell, the bot waits this many minutes before buying this coin again, so it does not jump straight back into the same drop. Higher is more patient; leave blank for 60 minutes; 0 buys back with no wait. | number, min 0, max 10080 | — | Raise it if the bot sells on a signal and buys straight back into the same decline. Leave blank for 60 minutes. | No buy on this coin for this long after a signal-driven sell. `0` means it can re-buy immediately, which in a downtrend repeats the same losing round trip. |

**Fees**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fees.takerBps`<br/>Taker Bps | The fee Binance takes on each buy or sell (spot is about 0.1%). Match it to your account: set it too low and backtests will look more profitable than real trading. The bot counts a round trip so a profit-taking sell never books a loss after fees. | text | `0` | Set it before your first backtest, to your real Binance spot fee — about 10 bps at VIP0, less with the BNB discount. | Left at `0`, every backtest overstates profit and the minimum-profit floor lets exits book a loss. This is one of the most consequential settings on the page. |
| `fees.makerBps`<br/>Maker Bps | The fee for orders that rest on the book rather than filling instantly. Backtests use it for limit-order fills; live trading uses the taker fee above. Match it to your account. | text | `0` | Set it alongside the taker fee. At VIP0 the two are equal. | Used for resting limit fills in backtests. Live trading charges the taker fee. Setting it below your real fee makes maker mode look better than it is. |

**Execution**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `execution.entryMode`<br/>Entry Mode | How the bot places your buys. "market" buys instantly at the going price and pays the taker fee. "maker" rests a patient limit buy just below the price so you save the spread and slippage, but it only fills if price comes down to it. At Binance VIP0 both fees are equal, so maker trades a cheaper fill for less certainty — backtest it before going live. | `market`, `maker` | `market` | Switch to `maker` only after a backtest of the maker config beats market for your pair. It does not lower your fee at VIP0. | `maker` saves the spread and slippage but risks never filling. Changing this changes the config fingerprint, so the profile needs a fresh backtest before it can go live. |
| `execution.makerOffsetBps`<br/>Maker Offset Bps | For maker buys: how far below the current price to rest the order. 0 rests right at the price; a larger offset rests deeper, so the buy is cheaper but less likely to fill. Ignored unless entry mode is "maker". | text | `0` | Only in `maker` mode. Use a small positive value rather than `0` if you want the order to genuinely rest on the book. | At `0` the order can match immediately and fill as a taker anyway. A large offset on a low-priced coin can fall below the exchange minimum and silently become a market buy. |
| `execution.entryTimeoutBars`<br/>Entry Timeout Bars | For maker buys: if a resting buy has not filled after this many candles, cancel it so the next tick can re-price it to the current market instead of sitting at a stale price. 0 leaves it resting until it fills. Ignored for market buys, which fill immediately. | number, min 0, max 9007199254740991 | `0` | Only in `maker` mode. Set it so a patient buy cannot sit at a price the market has walked away from. | An unfilled resting buy is cancelled after this many closed candles and re-priced next tick. `0` leaves it resting indefinitely, even if price runs far above it. |
